A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BFtS research, with substantial overlapping methods and experiments. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures support comparison throughout. v1 has no separate appendix; v2 includes readable supplementary material in Sections 5.1–5.6.

before.justification: Section 3 reports original synthetic-graph experiments and results on BAIL, CREDIT and GERMAN, including baseline comparisons, loss ablations and sensitivity to observed sensitive attributes.

after.justification: Sections 3 and 5 report original simulations and evaluations on four real datasets, including NBA, together with LDAM ablations and hyperparameter sensitivity results.

M1.justification: v1 uses LDAM for classification, cross-entropy for imputation, and covariance regularization in the classifier and imputer objectives. v2 extends LDAM to imputation, removes the covariance component, and reformulates the adversarial loss using group-conditional expectations (Section 2.3). These materially change training despite retaining the three-player architecture.

E1.justification: v2 adds NBA salary classification with nationality as the sensitive attribute, extending beyond the retained BAIL, CREDIT and GERMAN populations. It also evaluates synthetic graphs across low and high assortativity, introducing distinct connectivity conditions beyond v1's fixed-connectivity comparison.

E2.justification: Vanilla, Debias, FairGNN and RNF appear in Tables 1 and 2 in both versions. The corresponding plots retain Debias, FairGNN and RNF. v2 newly describes Vanilla explicitly and extends existing comparators to NBA, without adding a comparison method.

E3.justification: Model selection changes from AVPR and F1 to AVPR alone (Section 3.4). Synthetic class blocks change from 700/300 to 600/400; the main simulation replaces the p = 0.5/0.8 comparison with an assortativity sweep at p = 0.7. These are substantive reported protocol revisions, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1's covariance/adversarial-loss ablation is replaced by LDAM placement ablations for classification, imputation and both (Table 3). v2 adds alpha/beta sensitivity surfaces and assortativity stress tests. The 20–50% observed-attribute study remains as Figure 7, with NBA added, rather than being removed.

E5.justification: Both versions specify averages over ten runs and report uncertainties through ± values and error bars. v2 rounds displayed uncertainties more coarsely, but documents no change to run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimation or significance testing.

E6.justification: v2 adds NBA and assortativity results and replaces the loss-ablation entries. Table 1 also changes values beyond rounding: Vanilla's BAIL F1 changes from 0.73 to 0.88, Debias's BAIL %EQOP from 3.5 to 4.5, and BFtS's GERMAN F1 from 0.71 to 0.74. Revised objectives and selection criteria prevent treating these as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: New Section 2.4 and Appendix 5.3 introduce a minimax Jensen–Shannon divergence derivation, a demographic-parity theorem, a comparison corollary and proofs. v1 contains method and metric equations but no corresponding formal guarantees. Section 2.1 also narrows the observed-sensitive-attribute set from a subset of all nodes to a subset of labeled nodes.

C1.justification: The original worst-case imputation and fairness–accuracy claims remain. v2 adds theoretical robustness to adversarial-training convergence problems as an explicit introduction contribution and conclusion claim, substantially extending the claimed contribution beyond v1's method and empirical evidence.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a convergence explanation involving inaccurate independent imputations, vanishing gradients and collapse, connecting it to low-assortativity experiments. It explicitly limits its guarantee to worst-case imputations rather than true sensitive attributes. It also adds interpretations of LDAM placement and missing-race Black nodes' predictions in the PCA analysis.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies Vanilla's cross-entropy objective and the alpha/beta sensitivity grid from 10^-3 to 10. Conversely, v1's explicit synthetic edge-probability matrix is not supplied for the revised simulations. The anonymous code-access information is unchanged and merely relocated to Section 5.6.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted discussion of fairness without demographics, prior three-player GANs, and GAN convergence, including Hashimoto, Lahoti, Chai and Wang, Nguyen, and Vandenhende. It compresses earlier method summaries and removes several general references, while retaining FairGNN and RNF as the central comparisons.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: dataset descriptions, pseudocode, GAT results and ablation discussion move into an appendix, while theory enters the main text. Related-work and background explanations are condensed, subsection organization changes, and the title and sensitive-attribute terminology are revised.

P2.justification: The document changes from one to two columns. Figure 2 is redrawn, the synthetic bar chart is replaced by scatter panels, NBA expands tables and plots, and new sensitivity surfaces appear. The GAT table and observed-attribute plot move to the appendix; PCA markers and captions are revised.

improvement.justification: NBA coverage and targeted LDAM and parameter analyses broaden the empirical evidence. However, the new convergence discussion incorrectly assigns zero Jensen–Shannon divergence to disjoint-support distributions (Appendix 5.3), conflicting with its own theorem proof. New Figure 3 plots negative 1−DP values despite Equation 9's bounded definition, and Table 1's NBA accuracy-superiority caption contradicts Vanilla's higher AVPR and F1. These unresolved problems in the added theoretical and empirical support make the net quality benefit uncertain.
